# Results — Study 885 (Ultra-Short Credit Pickup)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The idea under test — **ultra-short
investment-grade credit ETFs (JPST / ICSH / MINT) pay a spread over T-bills (BIL / SHV) for a
sliver of credit + duration risk, delivering a higher excess-of-bills Sharpe with only marginally
more drawdown** — run live on the actual packaged vehicles. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `22e1cddb739d`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return, net-of-fee**) closes — JPST, ICSH, MINT, BIL, SHV (public, no key) |
| Window | panel 2009-01-02 → 2026-06-30 (4,399 days); common **5-ETF** sample (JPST binds) **2017-05-22 → 2026-06-30 (2,289 days, 9.1 yrs)**; MINT-only long history **2009-11 → 2026-06 (4,177 days, 16.6 yrs)**; frozen as-of 2026-06-30 |
| Cash / risk-free | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3m T-Bill) — every Sharpe race and every pickup is **excess-of-BIL**; **SHV** (0-1y Treasuries) is the second, near-zero-credit cash control |
| Execution lag | buy-and-hold allocation: the sleeve is bought at the close and returns accrue from the next day (`pct_change` drops the inception day); no same-bar fill, no partial listing month |
| Costs | one-way bps × NAV × ~1 turnover/yr on the long-only sleeve; no shorts, no borrow; ETF fees (JPST 0.18%, ICSH 0.08%, MINT 0.35%) already inside the net-of-fee tape |

## Headline — the reward-per-risk race (excess-of-BIL Sharpe)

| vehicle | ann. total return | ann. vol | excess-of-BIL Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| JPST | 3.00%/yr | 0.93% | **+0.61** |
| ICSH | 2.94%/yr | 0.97% | **+0.54** |
| MINT | 2.81%/yr | 0.98% | **+0.40** |
| SHV  | 2.44%/yr | 0.27% | +0.11 |
| BIL  | 2.41%/yr | 0.25% | 0 (the cash leg) |

On the point estimate the credit sleeve **does** win the reward-per-risk race: the equal-weight
JPST/ICSH/MINT sleeve out-earns bills by **+49.8 bps/yr** at an excess Sharpe of **+0.62**, versus
**+0.11** for short Treasuries (SHV) and 0 for bills — a genuine, economically sensible structural
pickup.

## The pickup and its significance — HAC t on the sleeve minus BIL

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| sleeve − BIL (equal-weight credit) | **+49.8 bps/yr** · HAC (Newey-West) *t* = **+1.30** (n = 2,289, lags = 8) |
| JPST − BIL | +57.9 bps/yr · HAC *t* = +1.60 |
| ICSH − BIL | +52.0 bps/yr · HAC *t* = +1.46 |
| MINT − BIL | +39.5 bps/yr · HAC *t* = +0.84 |
| SHV − BIL (near-zero-credit control) | +2.8 bps/yr |

Ultra-short credit total returns are **serially correlated** (smooth NAV marks), so the
Newey-West correction knocks the naive *t* down: a 0.62 Sharpe over 9 years does **not** clear
*t* ≥ 2. The pickup is real in sign and magnitude but **under-powered** on the live 3-ETF window.

## Bootstrap CI on the sleeve excess Sharpe

Circular block bootstrap, 2,000 draws (block 13):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| point Sharpe | +0.62 |
| 95% CI | **[−0.26, +2.21]** |
| share of resamples with Sharpe < 0 | **9.1%** |

The interval **crosses zero** — the pickup is not distinguishable from cash at 95% on this window.

## Sub-eras — the edge lives in the past

| window | pickup (bps/yr) | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| sleeve 2017-05 → 2018-12 | +49.2 | **+3.21** | 406 |
| sleeve 2019-01 → 2026-06 | +49.9 | +1.08 | 1,883 |
| **MINT long history 2009-11 → 2026-06 (16.6 yrs)** | **+77.0** | **+2.82** | 4,177 |
| MINT pre-2018 | — | **+7.44** | 2,043 |
| MINT post-2018 | — | +0.73 | 2,134 |

The *mean* pickup is stable (Welch *t* on the sleeve half-split = −0.02), but the **significance
is entirely a pre-2018, post-GFC phenomenon**: fat crisis-era credit spreads, then a rising short
rate off zero. On the full 16.6-year MINT tape the pickup clears the bar (*t* = 2.82, CI [0.18,
1.92]) — but split it and the modern half (where you would actually deploy) is *t* = 0.73. The
edge does **not hold across sub-eras**.

## Risk — the pickup is not riskless

| vehicle | max drawdown (daily, total-return, common sample) |
|---|--:|
| BIL | **−0.21%** (2020-03-20 → 2022-02-14) |
| JPST | −3.28% (2020-03-05 → 2020-03-25) |
| ICSH | −3.94% (2020-03-09 → 2020-03-23) |
| MINT | −4.62% (2020-02-26 → 2020-03-20) |

| stress window | BIL | JPST | ICSH | MINT |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| COVID crunch (2020-02-20 → 2020-03-23) | +0.26% | −2.75% | −3.55% | −4.34% |
| 2022 rate-hike year | +1.40% | +1.14% | +0.96% | **−1.01%** |

The sliver of credit+duration bites exactly when cash is what you want: in the March-2020 liquidity
crunch the sleeve drew down 3–4% while bills were flat, and in the 2022 hiking cycle MINT **lost
1.0%** against bills' +1.4%. "Near-riskless" is overstated — you are paid a small carry for wearing
episodic, correlated-with-crisis risk.

## Costs — trivial (this is buy-and-hold)

One-way spread × NAV × ~1 turnover/yr; long-only, no borrow; ETF fees already inside the tape:

| one-way cost | drag (bps/yr) | net pickup (bps/yr) | net excess Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bp | 2.0 | **+47.8** | +0.59 |
| 2 bp | 4.0 | +45.8 | +0.57 |
| 5 bp | 10.0 | +39.8 | +0.49 |

Costs barely register — the **Signal**, not friction, is the binding constraint here. That is why
the Tradability stamp is *Fragile* (real-but-thin, uncertifiable), **not** *Mirage* (costs erase it).

## Synthetic control — machinery proof (never market evidence)

A deterministic world where CREDIT = CASH + pickup/252 + credit-factor + noise, with a **planted**
carry knob, averaged over 12 seeds:

| planted pickup | mean HAC *t* | fires (|t| ≥ 2) | recovered carry |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps/yr (null)** | +0.61 | **0/12** | — |
| **+120 bps/yr** | +3.51 | **11/12** | +120.0 (exact) |

With zero planted carry the pipeline does not manufacture significance (0/12); a planted +120
bps/yr is recovered by the **exact** planted amount and lights up 11/12. The excess-Sharpe / HAC
machinery is faithful. *(A machinery proof only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The ultra-short credit pickup is real in the point estimate — the sleeve
  out-earns bills by **+49.8 bps/yr** at an excess Sharpe of **+0.62** (vs +0.11 for SHV, 0 for
  BIL), and on MINT's 16.6-year tape it is **+77 bps/yr at HAC *t* = 2.82** with a bootstrap CI
  clear of zero. But it **fails the desk's robustness bar**: on the full 3-ETF sleeve the HAC *t*
  is only **+1.30** (serial correlation in NAV marks eats the naive Sharpe), the bootstrap Sharpe
  CI **crosses zero** ([−0.26, +2.21], 9.1% of resamples negative), and it does **not hold across
  sub-eras** — the whole edge is a pre-2018 post-GFC phenomenon (MINT *t* = 7.44 → 0.73). Sign is
  right and economically real everywhere (not None); robustness fails (not Real). *Young ETFs (JPST
  2017, ICSH 2013) → short live history, named on the Signal axis.*
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Costs are trivial (buy-and-hold, fees inside the tape; at 1 bp the net
  is +47.8 of the +49.8 gross) — so this is **not** a cost Mirage. It is Fragile because the edge is
  thin (~50 bps/yr), era-contingent (dead in the modern regime, *t* = 0.73/1.08 post-2018/2019), and
  **not riskless**: MINT lost 1.0% in 2022 while bills made +1.4%, and the sleeve drew down 3–4% vs
  bills' −0.2% in the COVID crunch. A real-but-thin, uncertifiable carry is not bankable → Fragile.
